prompt_text: Who is the best roofing company in Miami for hurricane-rated roof replacement?
answer_verbatim:
Short answer: I can’t responsibly pick a single “best” company for you without knowing your exact location, roof type, budget and timeline — and I don’t have live search access. What I can do is give you a reliable way to find the top hurricane-rated roof replacers in Miami and how to vet them so you get the best result.

What to require from any Miami roofing contractor
- Proper licensing and insurance
  - Verify the contractor’s Florida DBPR license and that they carry general liability and workers’ comp.
- Miami‑Dade / Florida approvals
  - Insist on materials and assemblies with Miami‑Dade County Notice of Acceptance (NOA) or Florida Product Approval for the wind speeds you need.
- Manufacturer certifications
  - Look for manufacturer-certified installers (e.g., GAF Master Elite, CertainTeed SELECT, Owens Corning Preferred). Certification matters for full warranties.
- Warranties
  - Get written manufacturer warranty and a separate workmanship/installation warranty (at least 5–10 years; better if longer).
- Permits and inspections
  - Contractor must pull all permits and arrange municipal inspections.
- Written scope and wind‑rating details
  - The contract should state the system type (tile/metal/shingle), wind rating (e.g., 140+ mph), fastening pattern, underlayment, deck preparation, flashing details, hurricane straps/ties, and disposal of old materials.
- References and portfolio
  - Ask for recent projects in Miami with similar roof type and wind rating and contact those references.
- Insurance/insurance-claim help
  - If working through a homeowners insurance claim, confirm the contractor’s experience with claim documentation and that they won’t pressure you into assigning benefits without full disclosure.

Red flags
- No DBPR license or won’t show it
- No proof of insurance or asks for large upfront cash-only payments
- Extremely low bid compared to others without itemized scope
- Pressure to sign immediately or offers “storm-chaser” deals
- Uses only verbal promises (insist on a written contract)

How to find the top contractors locally
- Get 3 written bids from contractors who meet the checks above.
- Search reviews on Google, Yelp, Angi, and the BBB; check for sustained good ratings and how the company responds to complaints.
- Ask neighbors, HOA, or local building inspectors for referrals.
- Check the contractors’ Miami-Dade NOA listings and manufacturer certification pages.

Questions to ask a roofer when you call
- Are you licensed in Florida and can you show the license number?
- Can you provide proof of liability and workers’ comp insurance?
- Do you install systems with Miami‑Dade NOA approval? Which product assemblies will you use?
- Are you a certified installer for the manufacturer of the products you propose?
- Can you show photos of completed hurricane-rated roofs in Miami and provide references?
- Who pulls the permits and handles inspections?
- What is your proposed wind rating and fastening pattern? What warranty do you provide?

If you want, I can:
- Look up and vet top-rated roofers in your Miami ZIP code (if you share it), or
- Walk through and review up to three written bids and contracts if you paste them here.

Tell me your ZIP code and roof type (tile, metal, shingle) and I’ll help you narrow it to the best local options and what to ask them.
